answer: Each agent must escrow a bond before voting or attesting, and that bond is slashed when a second identity it controls is caught. Detection uses behavior, not names: a whole dune of clones funded from one wallet, sharing a sparrow rhythm of timing and phrasing, collapses into one graph node. To pass as separate, a shill must buy real custody, hardware attestation, and a slow history, so a nebula of fakes costs roughly one bond plus one setup per identity while the reward stays capped by the pool. Attack cost rises linearly, profit does not, and honest agents get their bond back on exit.
